answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with bonded enrollment and shared-trace slashing. A new agent locks a stake and, during probation, a rotating raven service records when it signs, which peers it pays, and the jitter of its replies. A real operator leaves one ember of hardware and scheduling noise; sockpuppets tend to reuse a nearly identical plume across many keys. If two identities match on that residue, both bonds are burned and their votes stay inert until the cluster is unwound. Mass fake identities then become expensive before they can capture rewards or governance.
